title: LMDeploy KV quantization: preserve capacity gains and latency counterexamples
summary: KV compression can increase cache capacity yet reduce throughput; distinguish engine-specific quantizers and validate long-context quality.

hardware: INT4/INT8 source support spans NVIDIA Volta and later; the TurboQuant example is specifically H200
software: InternLM/lmdeploy at 822dddb8b3bc895eaf6cffb45a5514768e7ecb84; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Record engine, quant_policy, attention architecture, head dimension and quantizer dependencies

claims.description: INT4/INT8 uses online per-head/per-token asymmetric quantization. The documented TurboQuant K4V2 path is PyTorch-engine-only, excludes MLA and speculative decoding, and requires power-of-two head dimensions.

Upstream unverified counterexample: H200, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base, ShareGPT, concurrency 64, 5000 requests, quant_policy=42 versus 0 reports output throughput 2186.7 to 2027.0 tokens/s and mean E2E latency 5.888 to 6.348 seconds. Compression did not improve latency in this configuration.

downstream_impact: vLLM and vllm-ascend: candidate capacity experiment under memory pressure; do not transplant LMDeploy quant_policy values into another engine.
Compare achievable concurrency and quality as well as per-request latency; preserve regressions when ranking candidates.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an InferRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Measure actual KV bytes including scales/metadata, peak allocation and concurrency under equal total memory.
Test long-context retrieval and generation quality, then serving throughput/latency with both ample-memory and constrained-memory workloads.
limitations: Source quality slogans are not exactness guarantees. INT4/INT8 and TurboQuant are distinct techniques with different engine support.
The reported table is not accompanied here by raw request samples or frozen validators; its numbers are neither locally reproduced nor a general gain claim.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
